description.en-US: The method's stable identity, such as 'KIOSK_DIRECT_AUTO_REFUND'. Immutable and unique, because seeds, channel configuration and integration callers name a method by this string rather than by a database id, and a renamed code would repoint every one of them at nothing. Plainly unique on a required column rather than a partial unique: the partial builder scopes a required field by a nullable one, and a single-column partial would also cap the table at one NULL-code row (the same reasoning recorded for sales_channel.code).
The operator-facing display name, e.g. 'Kiosk Direct - Auto Refund'. Mutable: it labels the policy, it does not identify it.
Free text explaining when an operator should pick this method.

How the goods reach the customer, and the one field that decides which execution workflow runs. Only 'kiosk_dispense' carries a workflow today; the other four are declared so the enum does not have to be migrated when they arrive, and every code path that executes a fulfillment refuses them outright rather than half-running. Immutable: the type chooses the workflow, and changing it under a live fulfillment would reinterpret its snapshots against rules they were never taken for.

How the first fulfillment target is decided. 'current_sales_outlet' resolves it to the sales point the order was raised at — a kiosk selling to the customer standing in front of it. 'customer_selected_outlet' requires the client to name a point before the order can be confirmed, which is what a mobile order picking a pickup kiosk needs. This is a selection STRATEGY, never a target: the target itself lives on the fulfillment and moves when the customer changes kiosk, while the method stays the same.

How many times one fulfillment item may be attempted before its outstanding quantity is treated as terminally failed. Null means no counter limit, which is what a customer-controlled method wants: the customer decides when to stop, not a counter. The minimum is 1, not 0 — a method allowing zero attempts could never deliver anything, which is what not offering the method expresses.

What happens once an item's remaining quantity is terminally failed. 'auto_refund' raises a refund for exactly that quantity with no human involved, which an anonymous kiosk sale needs because there is nobody to ask. 'customer_action_required' refunds nothing and waits: the customer keeps the entitlement and may pick another kiosk or ask for their money back. 'manual_resolution' parks it for an operator. Note this decides the policy only; it is never itself a status, and a refund it raises has its own lifecycle.

Whether the fulfillment target may be reassigned after the order is confirmed. False for a sale made at the kiosk the customer is standing at: there is no second kiosk they were promised. Reassignment is a business operation that moves the inventory reservation with it, never a plain field update.

Whether some items may be handed over while others are still outstanding. True for every kiosk method: a machine that dispensed two of three products has delivered those two, and treating the whole order as failed would take back goods the customer is holding.

Whether the method may be used only when the buyer's identity was verified server-side. It gates the policies that need somebody to come back to later — keeping an entitlement open, changing kiosk, requesting a refund — none of which work for a walk-up sale nobody can identify. Checked against the order's own customer_identity_mode snapshot, which the server calculates: a client that could assert its own authentication would be choosing its own refund policy.

How long stock stays reserved for a fulfillment before the reservation lapses and the goods return to the sellable pool. Null means the reservation does not expire on a timer, which suits a sale dispensed seconds after payment. A customer-controlled pickup needs a value, because otherwise one unclaimed order holds a kiosk slot forever. Expiry releases the stock and stops the fulfillment; it never refunds by itself — the customer may still reselect a kiosk or ask for the money back.
